question: In 1 Timothy 1:2, how does Paul affectionately address Timothy in his opening apostolic greeting?
opt1: Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith
opt2: Unto Timothy, a fellow ruler of the synagogue
opt3: Unto Timothy, an imperial scribe in Ephesus
opt4: Unto Timothy, a doctor of Mosaic law
correct: Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith
explanation: Paul greets Timothy with intimate spiritual tenderness, acknowledging him as his true spiritual son in the Christian faith. 1 Timothy 1:2 (KJV) - "Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord."

question: According to 1 Timothy 1:3, where did Paul urge Timothy to remain when Paul departed for Macedonia?
opt1: To return immediately to Jerusalem to consult the twelve apostles
opt2: To abide still at Ephesus, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine
opt3: To sail to Rome to petition Emperor Nero for religious freedom
opt4: To reside in Corinth to collect funds for impoverished saints
correct: To abide still at Ephesus, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine
explanation: Paul stationed Timothy in Ephesus to protect the church by confronting and prohibiting any teaching deviating from sound doctrine. 1 Timothy 1:3 (KJV) - "As I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine,"

question: In 1 Timothy 1:4, what two speculative distractions does Paul instruct Timothy to forbid because they produce useless controversies?
opt1: Roman civil codes and imperial tax decrees
opt2: Astronomical calculations and lunar calendars
opt3: Fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying
opt4: Public athletic games and military drills
correct: Fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying
explanation: Paul warns against mythic folklore and speculative ancestral charts that generate futile disputes rather than building faith in God. 1 Timothy 1:4 (KJV) - "Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do."

question: According to 1 Timothy 1:5, what is the supreme goal (end) of the apostolic commandment?
opt1: The enforcement of Levitical dietary restrictions and ceremonial washings
opt2: The intellectual defeat of Greek philosophical schools in public debate
opt3: The acquisition of material donations for building grand sanctuaries
opt4: Charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned
correct: Charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned
explanation: The divine purpose of all biblical instruction is authentic love springing from a purified heart, a clear conscience, and sincere faith. 1 Timothy 1:5 (KJV) - "Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:"

question: In 1 Timothy 1:8-9, how does Paul define the proper nature of the law, and for whom is it not primarily made?
opt1: The law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient
opt2: The law is obsolete in all respects; knowing that it was made only for ancient wilderness tribes
opt3: The law provides eternal salvation; knowing that it justifies every righteous man who memorizes it
opt4: The law is purely symbolic; knowing that it binds only priests serving at the Jerusalem altar
correct: The law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient
explanation: The moral law functions lawfully as an instrument of conviction and restraint against rebels and lawbreakers, not as a means of justification for the righteous. 1 Timothy 1:8-9 (KJV) - "But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,"

question: Why does Paul express overflowing gratitude to Christ Jesus our Lord in 1 Timothy 1:12?
opt1: Who hath granted me an earthly crown and political authority over Asia Minor
opt2: Who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry
opt3: Who hath made me exempt from all physical suffering and persecution
opt4: Who hath elevated me above all angels in celestial hierarchy
correct: Who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry
explanation: Paul gives glory to Christ for divinely empowering him and graciously counting him trustworthy to serve in the apostolic ministry. 1 Timothy 1:12 (KJV) - "And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;"

question: In 1 Timothy 1:13, how does Paul describe his past life before Christ, and why did he obtain mercy?
opt1: Who was an upright magistrate enforcing civic laws: but I obtained mercy through sacrificial offerings
opt2: Who was an innocent seeker of truth: but I obtained mercy because of my Jewish pedigree
opt3: Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief
opt4: Who was a skilled Greek orator: but I obtained mercy because of my eloquent prayers
correct: Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief
explanation: Paul candidly acknowledges his violent past as a persecutor of the church, magnifying God's mercy which met him in his blind unbelief. 1 Timothy 1:13 (KJV) - "Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief."

question: What core declaration does Paul proclaim as a faithful saying worthy of all acceptation in 1 Timothy 1:15?
opt1: That all humans inherently possess moral perfection needing only education
opt2: That salvation is reserved exclusively for the biological seed of Abraham
opt3: That external religious rituals guarantee entrance into the kingdom of heaven
opt4: That Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief
correct: That Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief
explanation: This foundational truth summarizes the gospel mission: Christ Jesus came to rescue lost sinners, with Paul viewing himself as the foremost example of grace. 1 Timothy 1:15 (KJV) - "This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief."

question: In 1 Timothy 1:17, what magnificent doxology does Paul ascribe unto God?
opt1: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen
opt2: Now unto the mighty Roman emperor, supreme ruler of nations, be praise and taxes for ever
opt3: Now unto the cosmic powers and celestial planetary rulers be reverence throughout the ages
opt4: Now unto the earthly priesthood in Jerusalem be tithes and animal sacrifices without end
correct: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen
explanation: Contemplating God's sovereign redemption evokes Paul's exalted praise to the eternal, incorruptible, unseen, and all-wise King of the ages. 1 Timothy 1:17 (KJV) - "Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen."

question: In 1 Timothy 1:19-20, what happened to Hymenaeus and Alexander after they cast away faith and a good conscience?
opt1: They repented immediately and were appointed as deacons in the Ephesian church
opt2: They made shipwreck concerning faith; whom Paul delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme
opt3: They relocated to Athens and founded schools of Christian rhetoric
opt4: They were rewarded by the Roman provincial court with civic honors
correct: They made shipwreck concerning faith; whom Paul delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme
explanation: Rejecting moral conscience inevitably leads to spiritual disaster, necessitating apostolic discipline to prompt sobering correction and stop blasphemy. 1 Timothy 1:19-20 (KJV) - "Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck: Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme."

question: According to 1 Timothy 2:1-2, for whom does Paul prioritize that prayers, supplications, and thanksgivings be made, and for what purpose?
opt1: Exclusively for Christian believers; that the church may overthrow pagan civil magistrates
opt2: Only for Jewish rulers; that the temple sacrifices may be preserved throughout the empire
opt3: For all men, and for kings and all in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty
opt4: Exclusively for the poor; that wealth may be redistributed equally across the provinces
correct: For all men, and for kings and all in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty
explanation: Christians are commanded to intercede for all human beings and civil authorities to foster social tranquility conducive to godliness and gospel witness. 1 Timothy 2:1-2 (KJV) - "I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty."

question: In 1 Timothy 2:4, what universal benevolent desire of God our Saviour is revealed concerning humanity?
opt1: Who desires only the educated elite to comprehend divine mysteries
opt2: Who ordains that pagan nations remain in perpetual ignorance
opt3: Who wills that salvation be restricted to a single ethnic lineage
opt4: Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth
correct: Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth
explanation: God's redemptive heart encompasses all people, offering salvation and divine truth indiscriminately to every soul. 1 Timothy 2:4 (KJV) - "Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth."

question: What supreme monotheistic and Christological truth is proclaimed in 1 Timothy 2:5?
opt1: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus
opt2: For there are many gods across the nations, and angelic mediators for each tribe
opt3: For there is one God, and multiple earthly priests serving as equal mediators
opt4: For there is no mediator needed, since human reason connects directly to deity
correct: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus
explanation: Scripture explicitly declares absolute monotheism and establishes Jesus Christ as the sole, exclusive Mediator between holy God and sinful humanity. 1 Timothy 2:5 (KJV) - "For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;"

question: According to 1 Timothy 2:6, what substitutionary sacrifice did Christ Jesus accomplish on behalf of humanity?
opt1: Who offered the blood of bulls and goats upon the heavenly altar
opt2: Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time
opt3: Who paid gold and silver tribute to Roman authorities to liberate captives
opt4: Who taught moral maxims without offering His life upon the cross
correct: Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time
explanation: Christ offered His own sinless life as the redemptive ransom payment purchasing liberation for all mankind, proclaimed at God's appointed time. 1 Timothy 2:6 (KJV) - "Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time."

question: In 1 Timothy 2:7, to what threefold apostolic commission does Paul testify he was divinely ordained?
opt1: A high priest, a civil judge, and a military commander in the legions
opt2: A municipal treasurer, a synagogue ruler, and a temple builder
opt3: A preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity
opt4: A legal scribe, a Pharisaic master, and an imperial ambassador to Rome
correct: A preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity
explanation: Paul solemnly affirms his authentic ordination as a herald, apostle, and authoritative instructor to the Gentile nations in truth and faith. 1 Timothy 2:7 (KJV) - "Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not;) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity."

question: How does Paul instruct men to conduct themselves in prayer everywhere, as stated in 1 Timothy 2:8?
opt1: Reciting memorized formulas while bowing toward Jerusalem
opt2: Standing in public street corners to display religious piety to onlookers
opt3: Offering incense while holding ceremonial weapons of defense
opt4: Lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting
correct: Lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting
explanation: The inward posture of prayer must match the outward gesture: pure hearts free from interpersonal resentment and free from unbelieving skepticism. 1 Timothy 2:8 (KJV) - "I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting."

question: According to 1 Timothy 2:9-10, what should characterize the attire and adornment of Christian women professing godliness?
opt1: Modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; but with good works
opt2: Expensive royal purple robes and elaborate jewelry to demonstrate church wealth
opt3: Pagan ceremonial veils decorated with figures of Roman goddesses
opt4: Austere rags of severe poverty to prove monastic asceticism
correct: Modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; but with good works
explanation: Christian women are exhorted to display internal spiritual beauty and good works rather than ostentatious, sensual, or extravagant outward display. 1 Timothy 2:9-10 (KJV) - "In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; But (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works."

question: In 1 Timothy 2:11-12, what apostolic order does Paul establish regarding women's learning and church authority?
opt1: Women are forbidden from learning scripture or participating in worship in any capacity
opt2: Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection; but I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence
opt3: Women are appointed to oversee all doctrinal debates and govern elder councils
opt4: Women are required to speak prophecies loudly above the congregation
correct: Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection; but I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence
explanation: Paul sets down order for church assemblies, directing women to receive instruction quietly and respectfully without exercising authoritative doctrinal rule over men. 1 Timothy 2:11-12 (KJV) - "Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence."

question: Upon what two creation and fall realities does Paul base his apostolic instruction in 1 Timothy 2:13-14?
opt1: Eve was formed before Adam in the garden; and Adam alone partook of the forbidden fruit
opt2: Adam and Eve were created simultaneously from dust; and both were deceived by the serpent equally
opt3: For Adam was first formed, then Eve; and Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression
opt4: Neither Adam nor Eve transgressed; but their descendants invented false worship in Babel
correct: For Adam was first formed, then Eve; and Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression
explanation: Paul grounds his ecclesiastical directives in creation order (Adam formed first) and the historical dynamics of the Fall in Eden. 1 Timothy 2:13-14 (KJV) - "For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression."

question: What reassuring promise of preservation is given in 1 Timothy 2:15 concerning womanhood, and upon what condition?
opt1: She shall be saved through legalistic fasts, if she never speaks to strangers
opt2: She shall be justified by temple offerings, if she tithes half her household goods
opt3: She shall attain immortality immediately, if she memorizes the genealogies of Moses
opt4: Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety
correct: Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety
explanation: The divine blessing rests upon women fulfilling their God-given domestic role in childbearing while abiding in faith, love, holiness, and self-restraint. 1 Timothy 2:15 (KJV) - "Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety."

question: According to 1 Timothy 3:1, what does a man desire if he aspires to the office of a bishop (overseer)?
opt1: He desireth a good work
opt2: He desireth personal political power
opt3: He desireth financial wealth and leisure
opt4: He desireth worldly fame in the city
correct: He desireth a good work
explanation: Pastoral oversight in the church is commended as a noble, worthy, and demanding spiritual labor. 1 Timothy 3:1 (KJV) - "This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work."

question: What core moral and domestic qualifications must a bishop possess according to 1 Timothy 3:2-3?
opt1: A bachelor who practices extreme asceticism, given to solitude, refusing all visitors, avoiding social contact
opt2: Blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre
opt3: A wealthy merchant of high social status, capable of funding building projects, trained in secular rhetoric
opt4: A military veteran accustomed to harsh physical discipline, quick to anger, imposing heavy church taxes
correct: Blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre
explanation: The elder must demonstrate irreproachable character, marital fidelity, self-mastery, hospitality, teaching capability, and complete freedom from violence and greed. 1 Timothy 3:2-3 (KJV) - "A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;"

question: Why must a bishop be one that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity?
opt1: Because Roman civil magistrates inspect every minister's private home quarterly
opt2: Because elder salaries are determined by the number of obedient children in the home
opt3: For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?
opt4: Because the children of overseers are automatically consecrated as Levitical priests
correct: For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?
explanation: Family leadership is the indispensable proving ground: inability to guide one's own home disqualifies a man from caring for God's spiritual household. 1 Timothy 3:4-5 (KJV) - "One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; (For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)"

question: In 1 Timothy 3:6, why is a novice (recent convert) explicitly disqualified from serving as a bishop?
opt1: Lest he fail to comprehend the Greek grammar of apostolic letters
opt2: Lest older church members refuse to pay tithes to a younger leader
opt3: Lest Roman officials view him as inexperienced in civil legal procedures
opt4: Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil
correct: Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil
explanation: Rapid elevation to authority risks puffing up a new convert with pride, exposing him to the same catastrophic downfall suffered by Satan. 1 Timothy 3:6 (KJV) - "Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil."

question: According to 1 Timothy 3:7, what external reputation must an overseer maintain, and for what vital reason?
opt1: He must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil
opt2: He must possess letters of recommendation from the Roman governor; lest he be arrested for sedition
opt3: He must be praised by pagan philosophers in public forums; lest Christianity be dismissed as vulgar
opt4: He must maintain commercial partnerships with merchant guilds; lest the church lack funds
correct: He must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil
explanation: A church leader must maintain an unblemished public reputation among non-believers to protect the gospel from reproach and escape demonic traps. 1 Timothy 3:7 (KJV) - "Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil."

question: In 1 Timothy 3:8, what foundational character traits are required of deacons?
opt1: Ambitious, eloquent in civic debate, eager for financial profit
opt2: Grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre
opt3: Silent at all times, harsh in judgment, avoiding interaction with the poor
opt4: Tolerant of deceit, fond of luxury, demanding personal reverence
correct: Grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre
explanation: Deacons must be serious-minded, sincere in speech, sober in appetite, and completely free from dishonesty or commercial greed. 1 Timothy 3:8 (KJV) - "Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;"

question: What spiritual integrity must deacons demonstrate according to 1 Timothy 3:9?
opt1: Memorizing the oral traditions of the Pharisees without deviation
opt2: Executing public punishment upon anyone who violates civil laws
opt3: Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience
opt4: Collecting ecclesiastical taxes from all surrounding villages
correct: Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience
explanation: True spiritual service requires uniting orthodox doctrine (the mystery of faith) with an unstained, genuine moral conscience. 1 Timothy 3:9 (KJV) - "Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience."

question: What double reward is promised in 1 Timothy 3:13 to those who have served faithfully in the office of a deacon?
opt1: They receive civic titles of nobility and tax exemptions from Rome
opt2: They are granted automatic immunity from all future temptations
opt3: They are endowed with gold and silver from the imperial treasury
opt4: They purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus
correct: They purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus
explanation: Faithful diaconal service earns an honorable spiritual standing before God and the church, alongside deepened boldness in faith. 1 Timothy 3:13 (KJV) - "For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus."

question: In 1 Timothy 3:15, how does Paul define the house of God and its solemn relationship to the truth?
opt1: The church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth
opt2: A temporary social society subject to the changing whims of human culture
opt3: An earthly political empire commissioned to rule sovereign nations by force
opt4: A mystical academy dedicated to speculative mythological allegories
correct: The church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth
explanation: The local assembly is the dwelling place of the living God, divinely tasked to hold high and safeguard eternal truth as a pillar and foundation. 1 Timothy 3:15 (KJV) - "But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth."

question: What magnificent six-clause confession proclaims the great mystery of godliness in 1 Timothy 3:16?
opt1: God created the universe from nothing, judged the earth with a flood, delivered Israel from Egypt, built Solomon's temple, sent prophets, and destroyed Babylon
opt2: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory
opt3: Christ was born in Bethlehem, fled into Egypt, was baptized in Jordan, performed miracles in Galilee, died in Jerusalem, and will reign on an earthly throne
opt4: Man was formed of the dust, fell into transgression, was given the law, offered animal sacrifices, wandered in darkness, and awaits physical resurrection
correct: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory
explanation: This early Christian hymn summarizes the incarnation, vindication, cosmic witness, worldwide proclamation, universal faith, and celestial exaltation of Christ. 1 Timothy 3:16 (KJV) - "And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory."

question: According to 1 Timothy 4:1, what explicit warning does the Spirit give concerning apostasy in the latter times?
opt1: All nations will abandon their pagan idols to embrace the Christian faith
opt2: The Roman Empire will adopt biblical law as the foundation of its jurisprudence
opt3: Some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils
opt4: The temple in Jerusalem will be rebuilt with stones from Macedonia
correct: Some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils
explanation: The Holy Spirit expressly forewarns of an end-times falling away driven by deceptive demonic spirits and destructive doctrines. 1 Timothy 4:1 (KJV) - "Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;"

question: In 1 Timothy 4:2, how does Paul describe the moral condition of the false teachers who propagate these demonic doctrines?
opt1: Speaking truth with boldness; possessing minds fully enlightened by classical science
opt2: Preaching the law with zeal; having hearts tenderly moved by the suffering of the poor
opt3: Living in total honesty; possessing consciences burdened by imperial oppression
opt4: Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron
correct: Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron
explanation: These deceivers are characterized by brazen hypocrisy and moral desensitization, their consciences cauterized as if burned by a branding iron. 1 Timothy 4:2 (KJV) - "Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;"

question: Against what ascetic false asceticism does Paul argue in 1 Timothy 4:3-4, and what theological truth does he establish?
opt1: Every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving
opt2: All physical marriage and animal food are inherently defiled by demons
opt3: Only vegetables may be consumed by those seeking true spiritual perfection
opt4: Food sacrificed to idols must be adopted into regular Christian table fellowship
correct: Every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving
explanation: Paul dismantles false ascetic prohibitions against marriage and foods, affirming that all creation is inherently good when received with prayerful gratitude. 1 Timothy 4:4 (KJV) - "For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving:"

question: In 1 Timothy 4:7, what are ministers instructed to refuse, and unto what must they discipline themselves instead?
opt1: Refuse the Old Testament scriptures, and study only Greek philosophy
opt2: Refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness
opt3: Refuse daily manual labor, and exercise thyself in political lobbying
opt4: Refuse church fellowship, and practice solitary monastic silence in caves
correct: Refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness
explanation: Timothy is commanded to shun unholy mythological chatter and rigorously train his spiritual life in practical godliness. 1 Timothy 4:7 (KJV) - "But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness."

question: According to 1 Timothy 4:8, how does physical bodily exercise compare with spiritual godliness?
opt1: Bodily exercise is sinful and destructive; while godliness guarantees immediate earthly riches
opt2: Bodily exercise is superior in value; while godliness affects only internal emotional feelings
opt3: Bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come
opt4: Bodily exercise and godliness offer identical benefits for both time and eternity
correct: Bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come
explanation: While physical fitness has limited temporal value, godliness produces comprehensive eternal blessings for both present earthly life and the life to come. 1 Timothy 4:8 (KJV) - "For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come."

question: In 1 Timothy 4:10, why do apostolic ministers labor and suffer reproach, and how is the living God described?
opt1: Because we seek the admiration of Roman senators, who reward our civic perseverance
opt2: Because we hope to establish earthly colonies, preserving our name for generations
opt3: Because we fear the vengeance of pagan rulers, who threaten our physical lives
opt4: Because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe
correct: Because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe
explanation: Their sacrificial labors stem from steadfast trust in the living God, who offers common providential preservation to all men and eternal salvation to believers. 1 Timothy 4:10 (KJV) - "For therefore we both labour and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe."

question: In 1 Timothy 4:12, what command is given regarding Timothy's youth, and in what six areas is he to be an exemplary model to believers?
opt1: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity
opt2: Let no elder rebuke thy youth; but prove thy authority through harsh discipline, heavy taxes, and public silence
opt3: Let no civil ruler judge thy youth; but demand diplomatic immunity through letters from the Roman Senate
opt4: Let no philosopher mock thy youth; but defeat them in public rhetoric using Greek mythological arguments
correct: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity
explanation: Timothy is instructed to overcome prejudices regarding his relative youthfulness by exhibiting exemplary speech, lifestyle, love, spiritual fervor, faith, and moral purity. 1 Timothy 4:12 (KJV) - "Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity."

question: According to 1 Timothy 4:13, to what three vital public ministerial duties must Timothy give attendance until Paul arrives?
opt1: To political rallies, to legal debates, to commercial trade
opt2: To reading, to exhortation, to doctrine
opt3: To ceremonial fasts, to animal sacrifices, to architectural building
opt4: To collecting civic taxes, to compiling genealogies, to physical athletics
correct: To reading, to exhortation, to doctrine
explanation: A faithful pastor must devote himself diligently to the public reading of Scripture, pastoral exhortation, and systematic doctrinal teaching. 1 Timothy 4:13 (KJV) - "Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine."

question: In 1 Timothy 4:14, what is Timothy exhorted not to neglect, and how had it been bestowed upon him?
opt1: Neglect not the monetary inheritance left to thee by thy ancestors in Lystra
opt2: Neglect not the Roman citizenship certificates granted by provincial governors
opt3: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery
opt4: Neglect not the philosophical scrolls presented by Greek scholars at Athens
correct: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery
explanation: Timothy is urged to cultivate and actively deploy his ministerial spiritual gift, received through prophetic confirmation and elder ordination. 1 Timothy 4:14 (KJV) - "Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery."

question: According to 1 Timothy 4:16, what dual focus must a minister maintain, and what profound result is promised?
opt1: Take heed unto thy popularity, and unto civic politics; for in doing this thou shalt gain wealth and fame
opt2: Take heed unto ascetic fasting, and unto physical seclusion; for in doing this thou shalt escape all trials
opt3: Take heed unto legal controversies, and unto endless genealogies; for in doing this thou shalt silence critics
opt4: Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee
correct: Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee
explanation: Perseverance in personal holy living and faithful biblical preaching secures the ultimate salvation of the minister and his hearers. 1 Timothy 4:16 (KJV) - "Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee."

question: In 1 Timothy 5:1-2, how is a young minister instructed to counsel and admonish older and younger members of the church family?
opt1: Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren; the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity
opt2: Denounce older men publicly; treat younger men as slaves; avoid speaking to women under any circumstances
opt3: Impose financial penalties on older members; command younger men with military severity; exclude women from meetings
opt4: Flatter wealthy elders; ignore impoverished younger men; treat all women with harsh suspicion
correct: Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren; the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity
explanation: Pastoral correction must mirror familial respect, tenderness, and uncompromising moral purity across all generations. 1 Timothy 5:1-2 (KJV) - "Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren; The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity."

question: According to 1 Timothy 5:4, what is the primary duty of children or nephews if a widow has family?
opt1: Let them transfer all financial care of the widow immediately to the church treasury
opt2: Let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God
opt3: Let them place the widow in a pagan municipal asylum funded by Rome
opt4: Let them sell the widow's ancestral property to finance overseas missionary voyages
correct: Let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God
explanation: Filial responsibility is a sacred Christian duty: children must repay their parents by supporting them in need before burdening the church. 1 Timothy 5:4 (KJV) - "But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God."

question: In 1 Timothy 5:5-6, what sharp contrast does Paul draw between a 'widow indeed' and a self-indulgent widow?
opt1: A widow indeed seeks civic remarriage immediately; but a pleasure-seeking widow retreats into solitary caves
opt2: A widow indeed collects temple tithes; but a pleasure-seeking widow writes philosophical scrolls
opt3: A widow indeed trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day; but she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth
opt4: A widow indeed fasting forty days is glorified; but a pleasure-seeking widow is excommunicated from the city
correct: A widow indeed trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day; but she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth
explanation: The true godly widow demonstrates prayerful reliance on God, whereas one pursuing hedonistic sensuality is spiritually lifeless despite being physically alive. 1 Timothy 5:5-6 (KJV) - "Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day. But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth."

question: What severe verdict does Paul pronounce in 1 Timothy 5:8 upon anyone who refuses to provide for his own family members?
opt1: He is subject to minor ecclesiastical admonition but remains in good standing
opt2: He has fulfilled the apostolic command to renounce worldly possessions
opt3: He should be commended for devoting all his income exclusively to church buildings
opt4: He hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel
correct: He hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel
explanation: Willful neglect of one's own dependents contradicts the basic moral tenets of the gospel, making such a person morally worse than an unbeliever. 1 Timothy 5:8 (KJV) - "But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel."

question: According to 1 Timothy 5:9-10, what requirements qualified a destitute widow to be enrolled on the church's official support list?
opt1: Not under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, well reported of for good works, lodged strangers, washed saints' feet, relieved afflicted
opt2: Any unmarried woman over thirty years old who made vows of perpetual silence and lived at the church door
opt3: A widow possessing substantial wealth who donated her estates to the Ephesian elders
opt4: A widow of Roman aristocratic birth who held civil citizenship papers in Macedonia
correct: Not under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, well reported of for good works, lodged strangers, washed saints' feet, relieved afflicted
explanation: Enrollment required maturity of age (at least 60), lifelong marital fidelity, and a proven track record of hospitable, sacrificial Christian service. 1 Timothy 5:9-10 (KJV) - "Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work."

question: In 1 Timothy 5:14, what pastoral counsel does Paul provide for younger widows to prevent idleness, gossip, and spiritual reproach?
opt1: That younger women take binding vows of perpetual celibacy and isolate themselves from society
opt2: That the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully
opt3: That younger women wander from house to house collecting donations for church expenses
opt4: That younger women seek employment as clerks in Roman municipal offices
correct: That the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully
explanation: To safeguard younger widows from spiritual ruin and avoid giving ammunition to enemies of the church, Paul directs them to marry, raise children, and manage households. 1 Timothy 5:14 (KJV) - "I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully."

question: According to 1 Timothy 5:17, which church elders are to be counted worthy of double honour?
opt1: The elders who possess the greatest personal wealth and social status
opt2: The elders who enforce the strictest legalistic penances upon offenders
opt3: The elders that rule well, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine
opt4: The elders who have served the longest number of years in civic office
correct: The elders that rule well, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine
explanation: Pastoral leadership marked by effective governance and tireless dedication to preaching and teaching merits abundant respect and generous material remuneration. 1 Timothy 5:17 (KJV) - "Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine."

question: In 1 Timothy 5:18, what two scriptural citations does Paul combine to prove that Christian ministers should receive material financial support?
opt1: The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof. And, Silver and gold have I none
opt2: Man shall not live by bread alone. And, Give us this day our daily bread
opt3: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse. And, Buy the truth, and sell it not
opt4: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward
correct: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward
explanation: Paul quotes both the Law of Moses (Deuteronomy 25:4) and the teaching of Jesus (Luke 10:7, cited as Scripture) to affirm adequate compensation for ministers. 1 Timothy 5:18 (KJV) - "For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward."

question: According to 1 Timothy 5:19-20, what judicial procedure governs accusations against an elder, and how are persistent sinners dealt with?
opt1: Receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses; them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear
opt2: Accept anonymous written petitions immediately; expel the accused elder without public inquiry
opt3: Deliver the accused elder to Roman civil courts; fine the accusers thirty pieces of silver
opt4: Settle all accusations in private behind closed doors; conceal all ministerial sins from the congregation
correct: Receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses; them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear
explanation: Elders are shielded from frivolous slander through the multi-witness rule, while unrepentant sinful leaders must be rebuked publicly as a sobering warning to the flock. 1 Timothy 5:19-20 (KJV) - "Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses. Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear."

question: What solemn warning does Paul give Timothy in 1 Timothy 5:22 concerning the ordination of church leaders?
opt1: Ordain every willing volunteer immediately, without testing their character or doctrine
opt2: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure
opt3: Permit only relatives of the apostles to receive ordination in the Ephesian church
opt4: Charge candidates a substantial ordination fee to test their financial commitment
correct: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure
explanation: Timothy must exercise extreme caution and thorough vetting before ordaining candidates, avoiding complicity in the sins of unqualified ministers. 1 Timothy 5:22 (KJV) - "Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure."

question: In 1 Timothy 6:1, why are Christian servants exhorted to count their masters worthy of all honor?
opt1: That they may receive immediate emancipation under Roman civil law
opt2: That they may be appointed as overseers of the master's estate
opt3: That the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed
opt4: That the master may be compelled to pay them equal wages with free citizens
correct: That the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed
explanation: Believing servants must demonstrate respectful conduct so that God's name and Christian teaching remain blameless before the watching pagan world. 1 Timothy 6:1 (KJV) - "Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed."

question: How does Paul characterize corrupt false teachers in 1 Timothy 6:5, and what command does he give concerning them?
opt1: Humble seekers of truth seeking divine enlightenment: to such give hospitality
opt2: Eminent scholars of Hebrew jurisprudence: from such seek apostolic counsel
opt3: Devout ascetics who abstain from all earthly food: to such grant elder status
opt4: Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself
correct: Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself
explanation: Paul forcefully denounces those who commercialize religion viewing godliness as a means of financial profit, commanding Timothy to separate from them. 1 Timothy 6:5 (KJV) - "Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself."

question: What paradoxical and profound spiritual principle is established in 1 Timothy 6:6?
opt1: Godliness with contentment is great gain
opt2: Accumulation of earthly gold with power is supreme wisdom
opt3: Ascetic fasting with severe self-denial is true righteousness
opt4: Intellectual brilliance with political triumph is heavenly reward
correct: Godliness with contentment is great gain
explanation: True spiritual riches do not consist of material accumulation, but of genuine godliness combined with inner contentment in God's provision. 1 Timothy 6:6 (KJV) - "But godliness with contentment is great gain."

question: According to 1 Timothy 6:7-8, what perspective on earthly possessions should guide believers?
opt1: We inherited eternal rights to earthly real estate, and must amass riches; and lacking luxury let us lodge complaint
opt2: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content
opt3: We brought righteousness into the world, and shall take our material estates to heaven; let us strive for gold
opt4: We brought the wisdom of our ancestors into life, and must buy monuments; let us covet costly apparel
correct: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content
explanation: The transient nature of earthly life reminds us that material goods are left behind at death; thus basic sustenance and clothing provide sufficient cause for contentment. 1 Timothy 6:7-8 (KJV) - "For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content."

question: What spiritual perils threaten those who are determined to be rich, as warned in 1 Timothy 6:9?
opt1: They become immune to all worldly trials and easily convert Roman emperors
opt2: They secure higher seats of honor in the coming heavenly kingdom
opt3: They fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition
opt4: They gain divine authorization to rewrite biblical commandments for commerce
correct: They fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition
explanation: The obsessive craving for wealth exposes the soul to deadly traps, irrational desires, and catastrophic spiritual and eternal ruin. 1 Timothy 6:9 (KJV) - "But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition."

question: According to 1 Timothy 6:10, what is the love of money, and what tragic end befell those who coveted after it?
opt1: The love of money is the sign of divine blessing: which enabled saints to purchase churches and live in perpetual luxury
opt2: The love of money is an indifferent human trait: which produces harmless ambitions and promotes civic progress
opt3: The love of money is the foundation of lawful trade: which guarantees salvation to those who pay municipal taxes
opt4: The love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows
correct: The love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows
explanation: Covetousness generates every form of evil, causing professing believers to wander from orthodox faith and plunge themselves into devastating grief. 1 Timothy 6:10 (KJV) - "For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows."

question: In 1 Timothy 6:11-12, what does Paul command the 'man of God' to flee, what six virtues to follow, and what fight to wage?
opt1: Flee these things; follow righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life
opt2: Flee manual labor; follow worldly philosophy, political honor, commercial profit; fight for municipal authority in Ephesus
opt3: Flee civil magistrates; follow ascetic solitude, perpetual fasting, silence; fight against physical marriage in the church
opt4: Flee fellowship with sinners; follow ceremonial washings, genealogical debates; fight for Jewish legal dominance in Asia
correct: Flee these things; follow righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life
explanation: The servant of God must actively run from the snare of greed, pursue Christlike character, fight the noble fight of faith, and tenaciously grasp eternal life. 1 Timothy 6:11-12 (KJV) - "But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses."

question: How does Paul describe the exalted sovereign majesty of God in 1 Timothy 6:15-16?
opt1: The supreme architect among many equal celestial gods, sharing divine honor with Roman emperors
opt2: The blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords; who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto
opt3: A mortal deity subject to the cosmic laws of nature, requiring daily sacrifices from earthly priests
opt4: An allegorical representation of the human mind, visible to all who master classical philosophy
correct: The blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords; who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto
explanation: This magnificent pastoral doxology exalts God as the sole supreme Ruler, inherently immortal, cloaked in unapproachable radiance, unseen and unseeable by mortal flesh. 1 Timothy 6:15-16 (KJV) - "Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords; Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen."

question: In 1 Timothy 6:17-18, what charge is given to those who are rich in this present world?
opt1: That they purchase imperial titles of nobility and build private marble sanctuaries in Ephesus
opt2: That they hoard their gold secretly in subterranean vaults against the coming day of tribulation
opt3: That they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God; that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute
opt4: That they separate themselves from poorer believers and establish an exclusive guild of wealthy saints
correct: That they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God; that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute
explanation: The wealthy are warned against haughtiness and placing misplaced trust in unstable riches, commanded instead to trust God and use their wealth generously in good works. 1 Timothy 6:17-18 (KJV) - "Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy; That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate;"

question: In Paul's concluding charge in 1 Timothy 6:20-21, what must Timothy guard, and what deceptive influences must he avoid?
opt1: Keep the legal decrees of the Sanhedrin, avoiding fellowship with Gentile converts who neglect circumcision
opt2: Keep the financial ledgers of the church, avoiding expenditures on the relief of widows and strangers
opt3: Keep the secret mythological codes of ancient philosophers, avoiding public proclamation of the resurrection
opt4: Keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: which some professing have erred concerning the faith
correct: Keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: which some professing have erred concerning the faith
explanation: Paul's final exhortation commands Timothy to guard the sacred deposit of gospel truth, turning away from empty chatter and pseudo-intellectual speculations that shipwreck faith. 1 Timothy 6:20-21 (KJV) - "O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen."
